transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-21 14:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Claire (CSM), Tom (Solutions), Priya (Eng Lead), Marcus (CTO), Rina (Security), Evan (ML Eng)

Summary:
- Focused on selecting a primary model variant for the pilot, confirming pinning policy, and rehearsing the rollback/fallback runbook.
- Discussed performance vs cost tradeoffs for the candidate models and compatibility checks (embeddings regressions called out).
- Agreed next steps: bench runs, cost sheet update, security docs, and a tabletop drill next week.

Topics covered:
- Catalog comparison of three candidate variants: redwood-gt-13b-int8, redwood-rt-13b-q4, and community-13b-fp16 (names in notes may be transcribed slightly off)
- Pinning semantics (hard pin vs soft pin with percentage traffic) and emergency unpin process
- Fallback ordering and emergency cutover timeline
- Audit/logging requirements for private deployment / V P C / on-prem scenario
Action items (recap): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay folks thanks for joining, we'll get started. I know calendar says 45 but we've got about 50 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya: Priya here. Evan here. Rina here. Marcus will be a bit late.
[00:12] Jonah: Jonah from Redwood, hi everyone.
[00:14] Claire: Claire, CSM.
[00:16] Tom: Tom from solutions.
[00:19] Maya: great, agenda is short: model pick, pinning policy, fallback rehearsal, and open questions around security logs. we'll run through bench numbers that Jonah collected.
[00:28] Jonah: okay so i ran three short benches on staging. i did microbench for 64, 512 and 2k token lengths, mixed batch sizes to approximate Citrine's traffic shape. quick takeaways: redwood-gt-13b-int8 is the lowest cost per token and consistent tail latency 80th percentile around 110-140 ms on our staging hardware. redwood-rt-13b-q4 trades slightly higher latency but better LLM quality on the prompt set you provided. community-13b-fp16 had the best raw throughput but showed higher variance and a couple of tokenization mismatches on a small sample (evan's notes match).
[01:02] Evan: yeah we saw the few hallucination style differences in the billing reconciliation prompt, nothing catastrophic but measurable on rouge-style metric.
[01:10] Priya: can you repeat the q4 vs int8 difference in plain terms? like what do we expect for us day to day?
[01:15] Jonah: sure. int8 tends to be cheaper and faster but sometimes loses nuance, particularly multi-step reasoning. q4 here is a 4-bit quantized pathway that keeps slightly more fidelity in certain attention heads; so your multi-step financial aggregation prompts scored better on the eval set. but cost goes up 12-18%.
[01:32] Marcus (joined): sorry, joining. caught the tail end.
[01:35] Maya: no problem. quick check — any hard policy from Citrine on deterministic output? i remember you want parity between prod and pilot.
[01:43] Priya: yes determinism is preferred for accounting paths. we cannot tolerate drift there. embeddings can have small drift but classification must be stable.
[01:51] Rina: from security perspective, we need audit fields for every call — request headers, user id mapping, model version, and the routing decision. also need to ensure KEK rotation with our KMS is respected; the private deployment option is likely.
[02:03] Tom: quick question on that — if you go private, are you expecting us to push full logs into your S3 or do you want us to integrate to your SIEM?
[02:11] Rina: we want native syslog -> Splunk; but a short-term S3 export is acceptable for the POC.
[02:17] Jonah: noted. on the pinning semantics: we proposed a soft pin (90% traffic to primary model, 10% to fallback) for first 48 hours after cutover with automatic circuit breaking if latency p95 hits >500 ms or error rate >1%. hard pin is available but requires manual override and is slower to revert.
[02:39] Priya: can we do immediate hard unpin if we detect embeddings regression > 2%?
[02:44] Jonah: yes we can add that as a rule. we'll need a small eval harness run to compute embeddings drift quickly. we have a lightweight comparator that runs in under a minute for 200 samples.
[02:55] Evan: is that the same tool that produced the drift numbers we saw in the sheet? there were two entries one labeled "embed delta" and a second called "cos sim" — which one should we use?
[03:04] Jonah: cos sim is the main signal, embed delta is an additional heuristic. recommend cos sim threshold of 0.03 for your workload as a starting point but we can tune.
[03:12] Priya: okay. Marcus, does that feel operationally safe?
[03:15] Marcus: yes, but i want an explicit cutover window and a rollback path that is under 15 minutes. that includes making sure network routing and DB migration steps are deterministic.
[03:25] Maya: agreed. so concrete suggestion: schedule cutover in a 2-hour maintenance window. first 15 minutes ramp to 50% traffic, next 30 minutes to 90% (soft pin), hold for 30m, if all signals green then promote to hard pin. in parallel run the embedding drift check every 5 minutes. if any gate fires, automatic rollback to last stable model within 3 minutes.
[03:49] Priya: that auto rollback time sounds optimistic, what's the failure mode? is it DNS change or traffic router flip?
[03:55] Jonah: traffic router flip — our control plane can route at per-route granularity. rollback is a control plane policy flip, typically sub-10s in our tests; the 3 minutes accounts for cascading retries and downstream caches (like CDN/edge). but we should rehearse to validate.
[04:12] Rina: for the audit log requirement, we need to capture pre-rollback model id and post-rollback id and the triggers. also timestamp with our timezone and user id mapping.
[04:22] Maya: noted. i'll include that in the runbook doc.
[04:25] (pause, someone shares screen - link to perf deck appears)
[04:30] Jonah: okay paging through the perf deck — slide 3 shows median p50/p95 for the three variants. note we ran with disabled persistent KV caching to get conservative results; enabling KV cache will reduce latency by another ~20% for your conversational flows.
[04:45] Priya: we need to know how much delta enabling KV cash (sic) would introduce to embeddings behaviour — any drift risk there?
[04:52] Jonah: KV cache shouldn't affect embedding vectors, it's per-request context. mis-transcribed earlier as KV cash. sorry. it affects generation latency not embeddings.
[04:59] Evan: small interruption — our preprocessor does some prompt rewriting, will that impact tokenization mismatch? earlier community-13b case had some token boundary differences.
[05:07] Jonah: yes that's likely the cause. we recommend aligning tokenizer version across the pipeline. we can lock to a tokenizer commit hash as part of the model pin so tokenization is deterministic.
[05:15] Priya: good. on model choice, i think team leans toward redwood-rt-13b-q4 because of quality on accounting prompts even with 12-18% cost premium. Marcus?
[05:24] Marcus: yes quality over cost for core accounting paths, but for chat summary/assist we can route to int8 cheaper variant. that implies a routing policy per route.
[05:32] Maya: that's exactly the routing policy we propose — route critical routes to primary pinned model, background tasks to cheaper variants. question: do you want automatic fallback ordering if primary fails, or explicit per-route fallback?
[05:43] Priya: automatic with an override button in console.
[05:46] Tom: we can set up per-route policies and also a single global fallback precedence list.
[05:51] Rina: and the global fallback list must be constrained to models that meet your compliance rules.
[05:55] Jonah: we have a catalog labeling system: "compliant" tag, "experimental" tag etc. we'll ensure catalog filters.
[06:02] Evan: small note — the community variant we tested was not marked compliant.
[06:05] Maya: so proposed pilot config: primary = redwood-rt-13b-q4 (hard pin at end of trial), fallback chain = [redwood-gt-13b-int8, community-13b-fp16 (not compliant, only for canary)] with strict catalog gating for prod.
[06:19] Priya: can the community model be used in staging only?
[06:22] Jonah: yes. we'll mark it staging-only in the catalog.
[06:25] Priya: good.
[06:27] Maya: let's rehearse a rollback scenario — Jonah, run us through what happens if the embedding cos sim delta rises above 0.03.
[06:32] Jonah: event fires -> control plane marks route unhealthy -> routing policy switches to fallback model per precedence list -> circuit breaker closes if error/latency persists -> we trigger hard unpin alert to oncall and place automated ticket in your JIRA via webhook if you choose to enable.
[06:49] Marcus: how do we verify that rollback actually restored correct behavior? we need a small canary test that runs post-rollback on the failed workflow.
[06:55] Jonah: we can embed a 50-sample post-rollback smoke test that runs in under 90 seconds and reports pass/fail. good idea.
[07:04] Priya: and who inspects the ticket? we want to avoid spamming oncall. can we set severity so only P0 events wake folks?
[07:09] Maya: yes; we can map thresholds to severity and even route to an alternate responder if you'd like.
[07:15] Rina: auditability again — every automatic rollback must produce a signed audit entry with cause and snapshot of inputs. how large are those snapshots? storage cost?
[07:23] Jonah: snapshots are minimal — we store input prompts, model id, routing decision and hashes of output (not full outputs unless requested). storage is configurable; default retention is 30 days.
[07:33] Rina: we need 90-day retention for POC logs and WORM support maybe later. we will discuss legal.
[07:40] Maya: okay we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[07:44] (longer section — bench numbers and slides discussed, skip transcription of every metric)
[10:12] Jonah: to summarize the bench tables — latency/cost numbers are here, quality deltas on your eval set are on slide 8. recommended starting config: primary redwood-rt-13b-q4 for accounting routes, int8 for auxiliary flows.
[10:27] Priya: i'd like a short A/B where 10% of real traffic is mirrored to int8 for 48 hours just to see in situ behavior. can Redwood do mirror + pin?
[10:35] Jonah: yes, traffic mirroring is supported. the mirror is off-path so it won't impact latency. we'll also collect logs for comparison.
[10:41] Priya: good.
[10:43] Marcus: other blockers? licensing?
[10:46] Maya: licensing is covered in the POC agreement; they'd need a contract amendment for Dedicated or Private but pilot is under evaluation credits.
[10:53] Rina: security docs?
[10:55] Maya: i'll send SOC2, network diagram and KMS integration notes by 12/24.
[10:59] Priya: excellent.
[11:02] Evan: one small technical ask: can we pin tokenizer and byte pair vocab to a commit? we need to be able to recreate outputs.
[11:07] Jonah: yes, tokenizer and model artifact hashes are part of the pin object.
[11:11] Priya: on the rollback drill scheduling — can we do Dec 28 at 10am pacific?
[11:15] Marcus: tentative ok.
[11:18] Maya: we'll send invite.
[11:20] Tom: last thing — cost delta table will assume 100k daily tokens, do you want us to rerun for your 300k/day estimate?
[11:28] Priya: yes please, run that.
[11:31] Maya: action items recap — Jonah will run the 50k/300k benchmark variants and share logs by 12/23; Maya will update cost sheet and send security pack by 12/24; schedule tabletop for 12/28; Priya to pick two canonical workflows to pin.
[11:46] Marcus: thanks all. if we can validate rollback and embedding thresholds within two weeks we're comfortable to push to a pilot commit.
[11:56] Maya: perfect. any final questions?
[12:00] Rina: no. thanks.
[12:02] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label glitches and small misrecognitions (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache, model variant names simplified). logs and slides referenced: perf deck (link: https://redwood.example/pilot/perf-deck), cost spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example/pilot/costs), security pack (link: https://redwood.example/pilot/security).

End of transcript.
